description: We are a passionate, multidisciplinary team building GlacierWatch for NASA Space Apps to monitor GLOFs in Gilgit-Baltistan using NASA POWER and Sentinel-2 data. Our platform features automated risk scoring, real-time telemetry, and Urdu emergency alerts. We are currently looking for enthusiastic teammates skilled in UI/UX design, frontend development (JS/CSS), or geospatial data analysis to help us build a life-saving solution.
summary:
GlacierWatch turns NASA Earth observations into a trend signal for glacial lake outburst floods in Northern Pakistan. For each of 36 glacial lakes, it tracks surface-area growth from satellite imagery, temperature anomalies and 72-hour rainfall (NASA POWER), and combines them into a transparent 0 to 100 risk score with a confidence value. When cloud blocks optical imagery, it switches to radar.

As a trend detective, it links separate Earth system signals (ice, warming and rain) into one picture, then tests that picture against a known event. In a replay of the May 2022 Shisper Lake outburst, which destroyed the Hassanabad Bridge, the score crossed the danger line on 4 May, three days before the breach. Control lakes stayed below 45.

Mapped escape routes and officer-approved alerts in Urdu and English turn the trend into action. As mountains warm, glacial lake floods are a growing risk, and remote communities often have only minutes to react. GlacierWatch aims to give them days.
details:
GlacierWatch is an end-to-end, satellite-driven early-risk indicator and multi-channel warning system designed to detect and forecast Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs) across high-mountain regions, validated on the Shisper Glacier and Hunza Valley in the Karakoram range of Northern Pakistan.

The system operates across four integrated layers:

  1. Multi-Sensor Satellite & Environmental Ingestion: Automated Python pipelines extract multi-spectral surface water indices (NDWI/MNDWI) from Landsat 8/9 and Sentinel-2 imagery to track glacial lake area expansion and ice-dam dynamics. Elevation and downstream slope profiles are modeled using NASA SRTM / Copernicus DEMs, while hydrometeorological and seismic triggers are continuously ingested from NASA POWER (temperature/melt anomalies), NASA GPM IMERG (extreme precipitation), and the USGS Earthquake Hazards Program.
  2. Composite GLOF Risk Scoring (risk_model.py): A quantitative risk engine fuses lake area growth rates, thermal melt indices, heavy rainfall accumulation, topographic dam geometry, and regional seismic activity into calibrated early-risk scores (glacierwatch_risk_scores.csv) benchmarked against historical Shisper GLOF events (2017–2024).
  3. Interactive Geospatial Dashboard (frontend/): A lightweight, low-bandwidth web platform (glacier-watch-sigma.vercel.app) displays interactive hazard maps, lake boundary polygons, historical surge/lake evolution trends, and real-time risk indicators for emergency responders and local authorities.
  4. Accessible Last-Mile Alert Dispatch (alerts.py): When a basin crosses critical risk thresholds, the backend logs every trigger in an auditable trail (dispatch_audit_log.jsonl) and generates localized Urdu audio alerts (audio_cache/*.mp3) alongside visual warnings so downstream communities—regardless of literacy level—can act immediately.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Actionable Early Warning Window: Shifts disaster response from reactive post-flood rescue to proactive preparedness, giving vulnerable downstream villages (such as Hassanabad and communities along the Karakoram Highway) critical lead time to evacuate and protect infrastructure.
  • Zero-Hardware Scalability: Relies entirely on open-access Earth observation satellites and meteorological telemetry rather than expensive, hard-to-maintain in-situ sensors in extreme high-altitude terrain, making it immediately scalable across the Hindu Kush–Karakoram–Himalaya (HKH) belt and other glaciated regions worldwide.
  • Inclusive Community Reach: Delivers localized Urdu voice alerts alongside an intuitive map interface, bridging the communication gap between scientific remote-sensing outputs and at-risk rural residents.

Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software Used

  • Backend & Geospatial Pipeline: Python (server.py, risk_model.py, alerts.py), Google Earth Engine (GEE) Python API, Shapefile/GeoJSON geospatial processing, and CSV/JSONL data pipelines.
  • Frontend & Deployment: HTML5, CSS3, Vanilla JavaScript (app.js, maps.js, api.js, data.js), interactive web mapping libraries, deployed publicly on Vercel.
  • Datasets & Telemetry: Landsat 8 & 9 Collection 2 Level-2, Sentinel-2 L2A, NASA SRTM Global 1 arc-second DEM, Copernicus 30m DEM, NASA POWER meteorological time series, NASA GPM IMERG precipitation, USGS Earthquake API, OpenStreetMap (OSM) infrastructure layers, and Figshare Glacial Lake Inventories.
  • Development Environment & Hardware: Standard consumer laptops running Windows 11 / Ubuntu (WSL2), VS Code, Git, and GitHub.

Creativity & Key Factors Considered

  • What Makes It Creative: Most GLOF research stops at static academic maps or dense technical bulletins. GlacierWatch bridges orbital remote sensing directly to last-mile human action by pairing multi-sensor satellite fusion with automated Urdu voice alerts and an auditable dispatch log—turning complex Earth observation data into a warning a villager can hear and understand in seconds.
    • High-Mountain Cloud & Terrain Constraints: Combined optical (Landsat/Sentinel-2) time series with topography-aware DEM slopes and non-optical weather/seismic triggers (NASA POWER, GPM IMERG, USGS) so risk assessment remains resilient even during cloudy monsoon or winter periods.
    • Low-Bandwidth Connectivity: Built the frontend using clean, lightweight HTML/CSS/JS rather than heavy frameworks so it loads reliably on weak 3G/4G connections in mountainous districts.
    • Historical Ground-Truthing: Validated our area-measurement and risk thresholds directly against documented Shisper Glacier surge and outburst flood events (shisper_events.csv) to minimize false alarms while capturing rapid pre-outburst lake expansion.
    • Accountability & Transparency: Implemented an immutable audit log (dispatch_audit_log.jsonl) and open-source data manifests so disaster management authorities can trace every alert back to the exact satellite scene and meteorological reading that triggered it.
